events.title: Dept of Consumer Affairs notifies Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026
events.whatHappened: The Department of Consumer Affairs has notified the Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026. The Rules provide for Indian Standard Time (IST) as the common time reference across the country for legal, administrative, commercial and other official purposes. The common time reference will support accurate time-stamping of banking and digital payment transactions, coordination of railways, airports and other transport systems, and also the coordination of emergency and other time-sensitive services. The Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution said that the Rules will come into force one hundred eighty days from the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. The rules are aimed at ensuring that important systems across the country use accurate and consistent IST.
events.whyItMatters: This matters to banks, consumers, payment providers, transport operators because systems that timestamp transactions or coordinate time-sensitive services may need to align clocks, logs, audit trails and operating standards with the prescribed IST reference before commencement. events.title: Standardised framework for classification and presentation of Schemes under the NPS
events.whatHappened: PFRDA issued Circular PFRDA/2026/47/REG-PF/10 under the PFRDA Act, 2013, creating a uniform framework for how NPS investment schemes are classified, named, presented and disclosed. It groups schemes into lifecycle-based options, Active Choice, NPS Sanchay, Multiple Scheme Framework (MSF) schemes, and Regulation 4A curated or thematic schemes such as NPS Vatsalya, NPS Swasthya and NPS MSME. Lifecycle options retain age-linked equity glide paths, while Active Choice permits subscriber-directed allocation across equity, corporate bonds and government securities within PFRDA limits. MSF schemes must be placed in standard categories according to their equity exposure. Pension Funds must use a prescribed naming convention that identifies the fund, NPS, the MSF category code and scheme name; Tier II products must say so explicitly. Subscriber-facing CRA and onboarding interfaces must follow a common selection sequence and display comparable information before selection, including launch date, historical and benchmark returns, charges, riskometer and assets under management. The circular also permits subscribers with multiple schemes to merge one into another, after which the target scheme's conditions govern the merged investment. Government-sector-tagged accounts are excluded. The circular supersedes three earlier PFRDA circulars dealing with fund changes, MSF introduction and lifecycle-fund nomenclature.

events.title: Directions under Section 35 A read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 – Ashok Sahakari Bank Ltd., Ahmednagar
events.whatHappened: It is hereby notified for information of the public that in exercise of powers vested in it under sub section (1) of Section 35 A read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) vide Directive Ref. No.S4110 /12-22-377 / 2026-27 dated August 28, 2026 has issued certain Directions to Ashok Sahakari Bank Ltd., Ahmednagar , (“the bank”), whereby, as from the close of business on August 28, 2026 , the bank shall not, without prior approval of RBI in writing, grant or renew any loans and advances, make any investment, incur any liability including borrowal of funds and acceptance of fresh deposits, disburse or agree to disburse any payment whether in discharge of its liabilities and obligations or otherwise, enter into any compromise or arrangement and sell, transfer or otherwise dispose of any of its properties or assets except as notified in the RBI Directions dated August 28, 2026, a copy of which has been directed to be displayed on the bank's website / premises for perusal by interested members of the public. Considering the bank's present liquidity position, the bank has been directed not to allow withdrawal of any amount from savings bank or current accounts or any other account of a depositor but is allowed to set off loans against deposits subject to the conditions stated in the above RBI Directions.

events.title: Industrial output growth expanded by 6.7% in July this year on annual basis
events.whatHappened: India’s Industrial output growth, as measured by the Index of Industrial Production (IIP), expanded by 6.7 per cent in July this year on an annual basis. The July data indicates that industrial activity continued to expand at a healthy pace, although the pace of growth moderated from the revised June level. The sharp upward revision in June’s IIP growth to 8.8 per cent from 7.3 per cent also indicates that the industrial momentum entering the July quarter was stronger than initially estimated. According to government data, Manufacturing, which carries the heaviest weight in the index, grew by 7.3 per cent, while electricity and gas supply posted an 8.7 per cent expansion in July. Water supply, sewerage and waste management rose by 7.4 per cent. However, the mining sector proved to be a laggard, posting a negative growth of 0.9 per cent last month.

events.title: Petroleum and Natural Gas Ministry clarifies CBG framework under GOBARdhan designed to provide stable price to CBG producers
events.whatHappened: The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas has clarified that the revised pricing framework for Compressed Biogas (CBG) under the GOBARdhan Scheme has been designed to provide a stable and viable price to CBG producers while ensuring that consumers do not face any material increase in CNG and household PNG prices. According to a recent newspaper article, the revised price of Compressed Biogas (CBG) under the GOBARdhan Scheme could place a significant additional burden on CNG and household PNG consumers. However, the Ministry explained that this conclusion does not present the correct picture, as it does not account for the Government’s affordability support and the substantially wider domestic gas pool over which the net cost of CBG will now be distributed. The Ministry explained that under the existing system, the procurement price paid to CBG producers is approximately 1 thousand 478 rupees per Million British thermal units, while the revised procurement price under the GOBARdhan Scheme is 2,110 rupees per Million British thermal units. It noted that the Government will also provide affordability support of 10 rupees per kilogram of CBG, equivalent to around 215 rupees per Million British thermal units with 95 per cent methane content, reducing the effective cost to approximately 1,895 rupees per Million British thermal units.

The sharp upward revision in June’s IIP growth to 8.8 per cent from 7.3 per cent also indicates that the industrial momentum entering the July quarter was stronger than initially estimated. Water supply, sewerage and waste management rose by 7.4 per cent. However, the mining sector proved to be a laggard, posting a negative growth of 0.9 per cent last month.

tracker.title: Standardised framework for classification and presentation of Schemes under the NPS
tracker.whatHappened: PFRDA issued Circular PFRDA/2026/47/REG-PF/10 under the PFRDA Act, 2013, creating a uniform framework for how NPS investment schemes are classified, named, presented and disclosed. It groups schemes into lifecycle-based options, Active Choice, NPS Sanchay, Multiple Scheme Framework (MSF) schemes, and Regulation 4A curated or thematic schemes such as NPS Vatsalya, NPS Swasthya and NPS MSME. Lifecycle options retain age-linked equity glide paths, while Active Choice permits subscriber-directed allocation across equity, corporate bonds and government securities within PFRDA limits. MSF schemes must be placed in standard categories according to their equity exposure. Pension Funds must use a prescribed naming convention that identifies the fund, NPS, the MSF category code and scheme name; Tier II products must say so explicitly. Subscriber-facing CRA and onboarding interfaces must follow a common selection sequence and display comparable information before selection, including launch date, historical and benchmark returns, charges, riskometer and assets under management. The circular also permits subscribers with multiple schemes to merge one into another, after which the target scheme's conditions govern the merged investment. Government-sector-tagged accounts are excluded. The circular supersedes three earlier PFRDA circulars dealing with fund changes, MSF introduction and lifecycle-fund nomenclature.
